what_its_for: Orlistat helps with weight loss in adults who are overweight or obese. It works by blocking about one-third of the fat you eat from being absorbed by your body. The blocked fat passes out of your body in your stool instead of being stored. It is used along with a reduced-calorie, low-fat diet and exercise program.
how_to_take: Take orlistat by mouth with each main meal that contains fat, or up to 1 hour after the meal. If you skip a meal or eat a meal with no fat, you can skip that dose. Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. Take a daily multivitamin supplement that contains vitamins A, D, E, K, and beta-carotene, because orlistat can reduce your absorption of these vitamins. Take your multivitamin at least 2 hours before or after taking orlistat, such as at bedtime.
dosing: The usual dose of prescription orlistat (Xenical) is 120 mg three times a day with each main meal containing fat. The over-the-counter version (Alli) is 60 mg three times a day with each main meal containing fat. Do not take more than 3 capsules per day. Your doctor will decide the right dose for you.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been more than 1 hour since your meal, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take an extra dose to make up for the one you missed. If you skipped a meal or had a fat-free meal, it is okay to skip that dose too.
storage: Store orlistat at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medication out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating high-fat meals while taking orlistat. Each meal should contain no more than about 30% of calories from fat. Eating too much fat at one time greatly increases your chance of unpleasant stomach side effects like oily or fatty stools, sudden urges to have a bowel movement, oily spotting on your underwear, and stomach pain or cramps. Avoid taking orlistat at the same time as your multivitamin — space them apart by at least 2 hours. Avoid taking orlistat if you are on cyclosporine (an organ rejection medication) — speak to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have: severe stomach or back pain, dark urine, yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems), blood in your urine, painful urination, or kidney stones. Also call your doctor if you have: signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or trouble breathing. Contact your doctor if you have rectal bleeding, severe or ongoing diarrhea, or if you are not losing weight after 12 weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: Orlistat begins blocking fat absorption right away, but noticeable weight loss usually takes several weeks to months of consistent use along with a healthy diet and exercise. Most people lose about 5% to 7% of their body weight after 1 year of treatment. Results vary from person to person. Talk to your doctor if you have not lost at least 5% of your starting body weight after 12 weeks — your treatment plan may need to be adjusted.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not use orlistat if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Weight loss during pregnancy can be harmful to your baby. It is not known if orlistat passes into breast milk. Children: Prescription orlistat (Xenical) may be used in children 12 years and older, but only under a doctor's supervision. Over-the-counter Alli is not approved for use in anyone under 18 years old. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease before taking orlistat. Diabetes: If you have diabetes, your blood sugar and diabetes medications may need to be adjusted as you lose weight — check with your doctor regularly. Thyroid disease: Tell your doctor if you have an underactive thyroid, as your dose of thyroid medication may need to change.
